findings.fix: Remove this rule, or replace it with a rule that does not hide `#main-content` based on orientation.
findings.violation: This rule hides the entire main content whenever the viewport is in portrait orientation, which is the default orientation for the vast majority of mobile phone users - making the page appear completely blank to most mobile visitors.

findings.fix: Remove `style="outline:none"` and let the default or a custom visible focus style apply.
findings.violation: Removing the focus outline eliminates the visible keyboard-focus indicator, which is especially harmful on the link to the accessibility page itself and violates WCAG 2.4.7 (Focus Visible).

findings.evidence: "Commuters can report a service issue by calling rider services. The change takes effect on the following service day."
findings.fix: Replace with content that actually describes weekend service changes, and de-duplicate the reused sentence pattern.
findings.violation: This text is about reporting issues and an unspecified "change," not about weekend service, so it does not match the section heading; it is also near-duplicate boilerplate of `s3-p2`.

findings.evidence: "Passengers should review the updated schedule through the mobile app. A confirmation message follows once the request is processed."
findings.fix: Write distinct, section-relevant copy for each paragraph instead of reusing a templated sentence structure.
findings.violation: This paragraph is nearly identical to `s3-p1` ("Local residents should review the updated schedule through the online portal...") with only the subject/medium swapped, indicating templated filler rather than section-specific content.

findings.evidence: `alt="A newly installed tactile paving strip along the platform edge."`
findings.fix: Move the image to the Accessibility improvements section, or replace it with an image relevant to weekend service.
findings.violation: This image describes an accessibility/platform feature, not weekend service; it appears to belong in the "Accessibility improvements" section (s3) instead.

findings.evidence: "Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicated sentence or rewrite it to be specific to checking real-time arrivals.
findings.violation: This sentence is reused verbatim in `s3-p2`, another sign of templated boilerplate rather than content tailored to "Schedule changes."

findings.fix: Add a `<caption>` describing the table, and either rename the heading or populate the table with actual schedule-change data.
findings.violation: The table has no `<caption>` identifying it for screen-reader users, and under a "Schedule changes" heading it shows no changes at all (both zones "On time"), which is confusing or contradicts the heading.

findings.evidence: "Local residents should review the updated schedule through the online portal. A confirmation message follows once the request is processed."
findings.fix: Replace with content specific to accessibility improvements; remove the duplicated template sentence.
findings.violation: Content is about reviewing a schedule online, unrelated to accessibility improvements, and duplicates `s1-p2` with only superficial wording changes.

findings.evidence: "Riders can report a service issue by calling rider services. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Write unique, heading-relevant content and eliminate the repeated boilerplate sentence.
findings.violation: Nearly identical opening sentence to `s1-p1` ("Commuters can report a service issue by calling rider services...") and unrelated to the "Accessibility improvements" heading.

findings.evidence: "Route adjustments take effect on the posted effective date."
findings.fix: Replace with a concrete statement, e.g. naming the actual effective date or linking to the specific adjustments.
findings.violation: This statement is circular/tautological ("adjustments take effect on the effective date") and conveys no actual information such as a date or which routes are affected.

findings.fix: Only render this status after a relevant user action (e.g., form submission), or remove it if it has no corresponding trigger.
findings.violation: This status message is shown with no preceding user action (no form submission or edit occurs before it) in this section, making it an orphaned/confusing message on page load.

findings.fix: Associate the button with a specific status element and mark that element `aria-live="polite"` so updates are announced.
findings.violation: It's unclear what status this button refreshes (there is no associated status region with `aria-live`), so assistive-technology users won't be informed of any update.

findings.evidence: `<div class="icon-delete" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Delete item" id="s3-customcontrol" style="width:16px;height:16px">`
findings.fix: Increase the hit area to at least 24×24px (44×44px recommended), and place it next to the specific item it deletes, or remove it if no such item exists.
findings.violation: This is a 16×16px custom clickable control, well under the recommended minimum touch-target size (WCAG 2.5.8 requires at least 24×24px), and it has no visible associated "item" or list for it to delete, leaving its purpose unclear.

findings.evidence: "Choose a plan" / "Enter payment details" / "Confirm your order"
findings.fix: Remove this wizard from the page if it doesn't belong, or if it is relevant, mark the current step with `aria-current="step"` and relate its content to the transit service context.
findings.violation: This multi-step purchase/checkout wizard is unrelated to "Accessibility improvements" or transit service announcements, and it provides no indication of which step is current (no `aria-current` or visual state).

findings.evidence: `check the current station closures` within "For the full list of upcoming adjustments..."
findings.fix: Make the link text, surrounding sentence, and href all describe the same destination/content.
findings.violation: The link text says "station closures," the surrounding sentence says "upcoming adjustments," and the href points to `/fares/history` - three different, mismatched destinations/descriptions for the same link.

findings.fix: State whether the field is required/optional and add `autocomplete="email"` for consistency with the phone field.
findings.violation: Unlike the phone field, there is no indication of whether email is required or optional, and it lacks `autocomplete="email"` even though the phone field uses `autocomplete="tel"`, making the form inconsistent.

findings.evidence: `<label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label">Phone number (required)</label>` with `<input id="phone" type="tel" autocomplete="tel">`
findings.fix: Add `required` (or `aria-required="true"`) to the input in addition to the visible label text.
findings.violation: "Required" is conveyed only as visible label text, not via the `required` or `aria-required="true"` attribute, so assistive technology won't programmatically know the field is required.

findings.evidence: `<input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true">` paired with error text "Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only."
findings.fix: Set `aria-invalid` dynamically only after validation fails on user input/submission, defaulting to `false` or omitted on initial load.
findings.violation: `aria-invalid="true"` is hardcoded in the static markup, so the field is announced as invalid to screen-reader users immediately on page load, before any user input or validation has occurred.

findings.fix: Add a disabled, selected placeholder option (e.g., "Select a route") so no route is chosen by default.
findings.violation: There is no blank/placeholder default option, so "Northbound" is silently selected and submitted even if the user never interacts with this field.
